title: Assurance that stays proportional to each behavioral change

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a way to keep formally verified software practical to change. Starting with a system whose behavior has already been specified and proved, engineers would implement a requested behavioral change and repair the affected proofs with effort comparable to the software change itself. Repeated functional releases would preserve the applicable guarantees without an increasing proof-maintenance burden. DARPA’s PEARLS program articulated the underlying goal of making proof maintenance comparable in effort to software maintenance.

Concept synthesis: the full proposal combines proportional proof repair with a separate requirement for structural stability. Across a sustained sequence of releases, selected measures of coupling and defects against the specification would not worsen. Proof repair concerns whether the revised implementation still satisfies its revised obligations; structural stability concerns whether continued development makes future changes increasingly entangled. Neither property automatically establishes the other. Here, proportionality means a bounded effort relationship under an explicit accounting rule and a defined workload, rather than a claim that every possible edit has a universally predictable cost.

significance.text: Software maintenance can invalidate formal proofs and require substantial repair work. A reliable way to contain that burden would make strong assurance easier to retain during ordinary development, allowing proofs to participate in the continuing release process. DARPA identifies this integration into normal development, with specialized formal-methods expertise reserved for the hardest cases, as a desired consequence of scalable proof repair.

Conditional impact synthesis: if representative behavioral changes could be implemented and reverified with effort proportional to their size, the direct benefit would be bounded marginal implementation and assurance-maintenance costs within the demonstrated scope. If structural stability were also sustained, a highly assured component could continue receiving features without a measured increase in coupling. This could make long-lived assured products more economically feasible and reduce pressure to choose between maintaining guarantees and shipping changes. These are conditional consequences of the proposed capability, not demonstrated economic outcomes.

Impact limits: proportional proof repair alone would not make total lifecycle cost proportional to behavioral change. Specification work, integration, tooling, deployment and architectural concerns outside the selected metrics could still grow. Nor does a preserved proof establish that the specification captures every user expectation: seL4 explicitly distinguishes its proved properties from expectations that those properties may not cover. A stable coupling measure would likewise provide evidence about that measure, not a guarantee against every form of architectural deterioration.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central missing capability is dependable, scalable repair of assurance artifacts through sustained functional evolution, with a measured cost relationship to the software work. PEARLS documents limits in the size and complexity of verification problems, the specialized skills required to use verification tools, and the repair effort that maintenance can trigger. PROVERS extends this agenda through tools for proof-friendly system design and reduced proof-repair workload. These sources establish substantial engineering challenges and research objectives; they do not establish that the combined SWE-05 capability is universally unsolved as of November 1, 2026.

Engineering synthesis: candidate barriers include proof dependencies that extend beyond the edited code and implementation relationships that make a local behavioral request require changes across many components. A practical solution would need to identify which obligations remain valid, regenerate or repair those affected, and check the resulting arguments. It would also need to accommodate intentional specification changes: changing the required behavior can require new invariants or contracts, rather than merely repairing a proof script. Non-local dependence and implementation entanglement are plausible mechanisms to investigate, not definitive causal findings established by the retained sources.

Measurement synthesis: the structural and economic parts of the proposal introduce additional barriers. Behavioral-change size needs an operational definition; code churn alone may conceal changes of very different difficulty. Proof costs must include expert intervention, automation and infrastructure upkeep. Structural metrics must be chosen so that apparent stability cannot be obtained merely by moving complexity outside the measured boundary. Even successful automation on many edits would leave the full proposal untested without these longitudinal measurements.

current_state.text: PEARLS provides a historical statement of the maintenance problem and the desired outcome that moderate code changes should lead to moderate automated proof repairs. Its retained program page is marked complete and no longer maintained, and does not report attainment of that full outcome. This omission is not evidence of program failure. The PROVERS page positively reports that PEARLS demonstrated AI and machine-learning support for generating and maintaining software-verification proofs at large scale, while describing further work on proof-friendly design and repair workflows.

The PROVERS FAQ dated May 4, 2023 reports a relevant AWS s2n example: over one year, corresponding proof scripts were corrected automatically after code changes in 953 of 956 cases, with proof engineers needed in the remaining three. This is substantial scoped evidence of proof-maintenance automation. It is DARPA’s account of the example in the supplied review; the underlying experimental data were not independently inspected. The reported counts do not establish the repair-to-code effort ratio, the representativeness of the functional changes, or a stable coupling trend.

The seL4 project reports no functional-correctness defects in verified code since completion of its functional-correctness proof in 2009, a history exceeding fifteen years. Its assurance applies to the verified configurations and the specified properties under the stated assumptions. This provides a strong baseline for the kind of assurance SWE-05 would seek to preserve. It does not establish correctness of unverified configurations or all surrounding system behavior, and the supplied evidence does not quantify seL4’s feature-development velocity, expert proof-maintenance burden or proportional repair costs.

On September 2, 2025, Proofcraft reported that seL4 proofs covered all Arm platforms on which the kernel could run at that time. It highlighted the addition of a 23rd Arm platform that required zero new proof work. This demonstrates valuable reuse and platform generalization within the reported scope. Adding platform support is a different change class from altering specified functionality, so this result does not establish zero-cost repair or proportional maintenance for arbitrary functional releases.

The historical software-aging citation supplied with the research cannot support its earlier detailed attribution here. The retained extraction of the page identified as Parnas’s “Software aging” contains only an IEEE Computer Society site label, with no substantive abstract or paper content. Consequently, the supplied review could not verify the attributed wording, detailed aging account or bibliographic particulars. This is an extraction limitation, not evidence that the paper or its argument is false.

Evidence synthesis: the retained material establishes meaningful progress in automated proof maintenance, long-lived formal assurance and proof reuse. It does not demonstrate the combined capability of sustained functional releases, proportional repair effort and independently stable structure. Because the supplied bounded search record is empty, this is a scoped assessment of the retained evidence rather than a comprehensive account of the field as of November 1, 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: begin with a production component whose verified properties, configurations and trusted assumptions are explicitly documented at an assurance level comparable to the relevant seL4 baseline. Pre-register a representative functional-change workload and a release count tied to a named five-year product-line comparator. The comparator should make the intended development horizon concrete; elapsed time or a large number of trivial releases would not alone establish representative functional evolution.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed effort test: for every release, require proof-repair effort to remain within a preselected small constant factor of code-change effort. Define the units and accounting boundary before the experiment, including expert intervention, automation costs and proof-infrastructure maintenance. Record specification work and implementation work separately, and report exceptional changes rather than hiding them within aggregate averages. The supplied evidence establishes neither a community-standard constant nor a standard release horizon; these thresholds would be explicit experimental choices.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed effort test

completion_criteria.text: Proposed assurance and structure tests: each released verified fragment must satisfy its applicable specification. Invalidated proofs or violations of retained contracts must block release until resolved. Intentional contract changes should create explicit new proof obligations rather than being treated automatically as forbidden changes. A pre-registered coupling metric and trend rule should show no secular growth across the workload. Any claimed absence of specification defects must remain bounded by the verified properties, configurations and assumptions; newly discovered mismatches should be reported and investigated.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed assurance and structure tests

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundary tests: make the release sequence, specifications, proof artifacts, tool versions, human interventions and cost records available for independent replay where access permits. Replicate the result with independent maintainers and additional components or change classes, documenting failures and scope restrictions. Successful finite trials would establish the breadth and cost behavior demonstrated by those workloads. They would not prove literal universality or an asymptotic proportionality law for all future changes.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and boundary tests

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: SWE-01, “Push-button verifying compilation for practical systems,” concerns obtaining implementation assurance through verification and compilation; SWE-02, “Certified synthesis of system-scale programs from reviewable specifications,” concerns generating certified implementations from specifications. Both could supply an initial verified system or tools for regenerating changed portions. SWE-05 focuses on the continuing cost and structural consequences of functional evolution after that baseline exists. Repeated successful verification or synthesis would not by itself establish proportional maintenance effort.

Roster-based synthesis: SWE-03, “Demonstrable adequacy of a specification against intent and the environment,” addresses whether the requirements being proved are the right ones. SWE-06, “Sound behavioral recovery of legacy systems,” addresses recovering behavior from existing software. These capabilities could help establish or revise the specifications on which SWE-05 depends. Maintaining a proof through changes neither recovers an unspecified legacy system’s behavior nor establishes specification adequacy.

Roster-based synthesis: SWE-04, “A compositional calculus for concurrent systems that fail,” and SWE-10, “Proof-carrying behavioral composition across trust boundaries,” could provide ways to localize reasoning and reuse component guarantees. Such mechanisms may reduce the proof obligations disturbed by a change. Their central concerns are sound composition under concurrency, failure or trust boundaries; SWE-05 additionally asks whether repeated functional changes preserve assurance at a bounded measured cost without worsening selected structural measures.

Roster-based synthesis: SWE-07, “Practical confinement of general untrusted programs,” SWE-08, “Sequential meaning for fault-tolerant distributed execution,” and SWE-09, “Observable determinism as the default for parallel systems code,” concern particular guarantees or execution models. Systems providing those capabilities could themselves need proportional assurance maintenance. SWE-05 does not supply confinement, fault-tolerant sequential meaning or observable determinism merely by preserving proofs; those properties must be included in the relevant specifications and demonstrated within their own scopes.

Roster-based synthesis: SWE-11, “Proved semantics-preserving transformation of practical systems,” concerns transformations that retain behavior, such as a migration whose semantics are preserved. SWE-05 concerns specified behavioral changes and the updated proofs they require. They may share proof-reuse techniques, but successful behavior-preserving migration does not establish proportional repair through functional evolution. Autonomous runtime repair of production failures and predictive laws of defect rates are also distinct objectives mentioned in the research, although neither has an entry in the supplied roster. No additional historical comparison list was supplied.

change_log.change: Preserved SWE-05’s identity and combined proportional proof repair with separately measured structural stability.
change_log.reason: The review supports a coherent capability while clarifying that verification does not itself guarantee stable coupling or architectural health.

change_log.change: Replaced categorical present-day openness and definitive causal claims with scoped challenges and explicitly identified engineering hypotheses.
change_log.reason: DARPA documents scale, expertise and maintenance barriers, but does not establish non-local dependence as the definitive cause or universal open status as of November 1, 2026.

change_log.change: Added DARPA’s positive account of PEARLS and the year-long s2n result of 953 automatic proof-script corrections in 956 cases.
change_log.reason: These relevant successes qualify the earlier account of limitations without demonstrating the full combined innovation.

change_log.change: Qualified the seL4 defect-history claim by verified configuration, specification and assumptions, and removed the unsupported characterization of its maintenance burden.
change_log.reason: The retained evidence supports the project’s reported history since 2009 but does not measure expert effort or proportional feature-maintenance costs.

change_log.change: Retained the September 2025 platform-generalization result, including the 23rd Arm platform requiring zero new proof work.
change_log.reason: The quantitative result is supported, but platform generalization must remain distinct from arbitrary functional change.

change_log.change: Removed reliance on the detailed Parnas attribution and preserved the extraction limitation.
change_log.reason: The supplied artifact contains only a site label and cannot verify the attributed substantive content; that limitation does not refute the source.

change_log.change: Narrowed the direct economic claim and made broader product-lifecycle benefits conditional.
change_log.reason: Proportional proof repair does not bound specification, integration or other lifecycle costs, and stable selected metrics do not guarantee complete architectural health.

change_log.change: Made the proposed longitudinal demonstration concrete through a named comparator, inclusive cost accounting, explicit contract-change handling and reproducibility requirements.
change_log.reason: These additions prevent omitted costs and ambiguous obligations from creating misleading evidence of proportionality.

change_log.change: Explained relationships to every other supplied roster entry and retained the distinctions from runtime repair and defect-rate prediction.
change_log.reason: The innovation shares enabling techniques with neighboring concepts while retaining its focus on assurance during functional evolution.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish whether the full combined capability has been achieved elsewhere or remains field-wide open as of November 1, 2026; the bounded search record is empty.
The s2n example lacks independently inspected experimental data here, including change composition, effort accounting, infrastructure costs and structural measurements.
The retained seL4 evidence does not quantify functional-release velocity or the human and automated effort required to maintain proofs across such releases.
Behavioral-change size, the five-year product-line comparator, the effort constant, cost units, coupling metric and trend rule remain to be selected for an executable demonstration.
The software-aging attribution and bibliographic particulars remain unverified because the retained extraction lacks substantive content.
Related-concept comparisons are based on the supplied roster titles rather than full records for those innovations; no historical comparison list was supplied.
